rejected.title: Ice-mediated interfacial membrane synthesis of cargo-independent microcapsules
rejected.reason: User-confirmed DOI exclusion: the principal contribution is ice-template interfacial membrane fabrication and cargo-independent microcapsule function, not the Gallery's general preparative organic synthesis methodology.
rejected.evidenceBasis: The Nature Synthesis publisher page was read on 2026-10-02. Its abstract describes monomer enrichment in the quasi-liquid layer of ice spheres, confined interfacial amidation forming a polyamide membrane, and release of cargo-loaded capsules on melting. It reports tunable capsule dimensions, permeability and multienzyme/photoenzymatic CO2-to-methanol performance. These are genuine covalent membrane-formation and biocatalytic operations, but the reported primary contribution is fabrication and function of semipermeable compartments. The user explicitly states this DOI is outside scope. Full article and SI substrate tables were not obtained in this recheck.
rejected.challengeReason: The strongest argument for the previous include is the real interfacial amidation/polymer formation and the demonstrated catalytic cargo. That does not establish a general organic preparative transformation or transferable polymer reaction/chain-architecture method as the main contribution. Counting membrane thickness, capsule size or cargo compatibility as organic substrate scope was the wrong boundary. The user's explicit exclusion supersedes the 2026-10-02 08:00 include without creating a blanket ban on all polymerization or heterogeneous catalysis papers.

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: Ice-templated fabrication of cargo-independent semipermeable polyamide microcapsules and their compartmentalization performance.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: Interfacial amidation forms the capsule membrane; this real chemical reaction is acknowledged rather than denied.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The obtained abstract discusses capsule dimensions and cargo compatibility. Those measures are not evidence for a general organic substrate-to-product preparative method. No unobserved substrate counts or SI claims are asserted.
scopeAssessment.sourceEvidence: Publisher abstract and captions: membrane fabrication/formation, cargo compatibility, permeability and encapsulated photoenzymatic catalysis. Publication date confirmed as 2026-10-01.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: Real polyamide formation does not automatically qualify a membrane-fabrication article; explicit user DOI exclusion and primary-contribution assessment both require exclusion.

note: Only previously confirmed out-of-scope entries are removed. This does not claim a complete new discovery audit or global semantic closure.
